speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It will have very severe implications for the world economy that is yet to recover from the pandemic shock.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Both Russia and Ukraine are also major food and commodity exporters.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, the crisis will have both a demand-side and supply-side impact.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Do we have further scope to moderate imported inflation with the stronger Singapore dollar and the other measures?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The other concern is the supply of oil and gas.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In particular, whether the conflict in Ukraine will disrupt the supply of LNG to Asia.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This would have implications on our energy security as LNG is our critical contingent source of energy.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I feel that there is enormous scope to manage down our consumption of energy and to cut wastage of electricity by both households and commercial entities.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For households, we can encourage more conscientious use of electricity, and it is often about reminding consumers on good habits.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Simple steps such as setting your aircon temperature higher, more conscious to turn off appliances like TV, lights when not in use, lesser use of water heater, for example, among others; all these add up and move the needle to save electricity.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In the commercial area, there is also more that we can do to reduce energy consumption.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Many of our commercial and office buildings are more than adequately brightened during after office hours and on weekends.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Government could also advise shopping areas, industries and other public spaces’ management to review their energy consumption and institute electricity saving measures.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I believe if the Government can take the lead in driving the overall energy conservation, we could achieve significant energy savings that can manage down the demand of energy consumption.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This would absolutely fit into the efforts of the Singapore Green Plan as well where we aim to reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask if the Government has any plans to mount an energy conservation campaign to encourage businesses and household to save electricity?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated growth in the digital sector and highlighted that firms, regardless of industry, would benefit from developing stronger digital capabilities.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How has the Government supported firms, especially local SMEs, in developing their digital capabilities?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Mr Chairman, it is not just the disruptions from external events but also disruptions from technological developments that our firms need to deal with.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Nonetheless, we also have forward-thinking firms in Singapore which are the ones driving this disruption through innovating and creating new products and services.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How can we spread this culture of innovation to more firms in the economy, including for more SMEs to start innovation projects?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How are we supporting the firms which are interested but may need some help in developing the needed capabilities to innovate?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This cannot be left solely to the industry nor can it be driven purely by the Government.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How would the Government work with the industry and workers to build a future-ready workforce?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The world has changed at a faster pace due to human-led developments like technological changes, innovations, climate change actions and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But the world has also become more unpredictable and less stable due to unexpected events like the pandemic, political conflicts, tensions and higher interdependent risks.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We need to remain even more agile to adjust to these expected and unexpected changes and events as well as the emerging new challenges in the overall economic environment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Against this backdrop, it is important for the Government to share how we intend to respond and position ourselves in this challenging landscape.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: To guide and align the different stakeholders in moving towards a common goal, can I ask the Minister for his overall vision of the Singapore economy?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The labour crunch is further exacerbated by a mismatch in skills.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Therefore, investing in the training and development of our workers has never been more urgent.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: There is great potential in leveraging a tripartite partnership to address workers' training.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The close collaboration between Enterprise Singapore and the industry and trade associations will be crucial to ensure that a sector-based training solution is developed for scalability.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The framework must accommodate SMEs which cannot achieve the scale needed to form CTCs.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Cheif Technology Officer (CTO), as a service scheme, was launched to offer SMEs access to a CTO to help them develop plans and technology solutions and even training programmes without the need for them actually hiring one themselves.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to replicate this to include other key functions, such as Chief People Officer as a service, Chief Sustainability Officer as a Service, to provide the expertise central to SMEs' transformation and pivot to new growth areas.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Companies can also tap on remote or offshore working models more systematically.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This has proven to be a genuinely viable option for some areas of work, such as technology services, offered out of Vietnam and Indonesia.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will open firms to a new channel of manpower by tapping on offshore talent pool to work alongside onshore Singapore teams.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, companies will benefit from support to navigate the offshore marketplace and for a framework to source and onboard remote talents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But it will take time for the impact of these measures to be felt in a large flow economy like ours while there are many nearer-term headwinds to global trade and economic recovery.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Competition for investments can also be expected to intensify, especially in a post-COVID-19, post-BEPS 2.0 world where companies are refining their global and regional games.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: EDB has done remarkably well during the pandemic years.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As the world emerges from the pandemic, how does the investment pipeline look going forward?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How can Singapore extract value quickly from the recently completed trade agreements?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Can the Government give an update on progress in facilitating cross border data flows and digital trade?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How else can the Government enhance Singapore's competitiveness in the near term to capitalise on opportunities, both amidst the COVID-19 recovery and in a post-BEPS 2.0 world?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I declare that I am a council member of the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants and working with a Singaporean bank.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In 2021, close to 70% of the nominal value-added to our GDP was generated by the services industries.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As of last year, the two biggest contributors were wholesale trade at 17.9% and finance and insurance at 14.6%.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are we doing to keep our lead in these two sectors?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The professional services sector and information and communications sector account for 5.8% and 5.6% respectively and show much potential for further growth.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Professional services, such as accountancy and consulting in information and communications technology (ICT) sectors, provide good jobs and career prospects for our Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry support local enterprise developments and attract international investments in these sectors?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Mr Chairman, last year, MTI announced a 10-year plan to grow Singapore's manufacturing sector, maintaining its share of about 20% of GDP.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: This is an ambitious goal, given that it has to take place while the global economy continues to be impacted by COVD-19 and, now, the latest challenges from the crisis in Ukraine – and all within the context of a tightened labour market.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Would the Ministry be able to provide an update on how we have progressed over the past year for the manufacturing sector?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Mr Chairman, manufacturing is a diverse sector covering many industries.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: While we want to spread our eggs across different baskets and have sufficient variety in our industries, we are still a small country and would need to focus on our strengths.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Would MTI be able to share what are some industries which Singapore has strengths in and what the Government is doing to develop these industries?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: To fully benefit from the growth of such Industries, we will need to ensure that Singaporeans are able to access good job opportunities in the manufacturing sector.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: This is not only desirable but also critical, given our tightening manpower constraints.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: How will we prepare Singaporeans for high-quality jobs in the manufacturing sector, both in terms of having the relevant capabilities to land these jobs and the desire to want to enter and stay in these industries?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: At the same time, how will we encourage the industry to hire Singaporeans for such jobs?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, trade and connectivity have been Singapore's strategic focus to ensure we continue to be relevant on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I have four points to make in the next few minutes.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Number one, Singapore as a key node in the global trading network.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Digital and green are two S-curves that will continue to disrupt economies and societies.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: It is right that digitalisation and green are both big agenda items in Budget 2022.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Meanwhile, we are seeing the weakening of the rules-based multilateral trading system and increasing disregard for WTO rules.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, we saw the escalation of unilateral and protectionist measures by many countries in their response to COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: There is the war in Ukraine and its implications on supply chain disruptions and escalating energy prices, which Minister Gan Kim Yong took us through the other day.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister for Trade and Industry give this House an update on the way forward and what might be Singapore's playbook for Singapore's trade and industry?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister also share MTI and EDB's strategy to accelerate and expand Singapore as a key node in the global trading network?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: To my second point – skills and talent 4.0.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: With the digital disruption and the impending green disruption, everyone needs new skills and competencies.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that companies' industry-led reskilling of the Singaporean workforce is the way to go.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Much has been talked about Industry 4.0 in advanced manufacturing.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Bosch Rexroth, an industry leader, decided to locate their regional training centre for Industry 4.0 in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: They partnered Singapore Polytechnic and co-launched the first course in 2020.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Another notable example would be Google's participation in Skills Ignition SG to train digital skills.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We need more queen bees like this to come forward and work with our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Our economic agencies, which have the best relationships and have the most influence with the queen bee companies, are in the best position to programmatically scale up our skills and talent 4.0 initiative.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister share how our Government economic agencies may support with carrots and sticks to strongly encourage the queen bee companies, multinational companies (MNCs) and large local enterprises (LLEs) to invest in our people to get to skills and talent 4.0?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The second proposal is to leverage on Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to strengthen the workplace learning ecosystems.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: When COVID-19 broke out, SBF Foundation, together with seven TACs, launched the Industry Compassion Fund to support employees in their respective sectors, who are having difficulties.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: During COVID-19, SBF also played clearing house for migrant workers from one company which cannot keep them to be matched with another company which needs them.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, strengthening the workplace learning ecosystems to address the issue of skills mismatch is part of the great manpower challenge for our businesses in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Considering that TACs are aligned by industry, and they should understand best the disruptions taking place in their industry and the skills their industry needs to stay relevant, TACs can, hence, be a platform to be leveraged in strengthening workplace learning ecosystems.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: There has been strong support by the Government over the years to build capacity at the TACs via the LEAD programme.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: It is timely to give TACs a booster shot to enable them to support their members with job development, job redesign, skills matching and broadening their understanding in sustainability and digitalisation and the new trends.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: TACs can also partner IHLs, NTUC, e2i and even queen bee companies to programmatically strengthen the workplace learning system uplift their skills, industry by industry.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: It would take a village to uplift an industry.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In my Budget debate speech, I put forward the fact that SMEs need capital and credit, talent and network.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In this speech, I will speak on access to networks.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Global Connect at SBF, set up by SBF in November of 2019 in partnership with Enterprise Singapore to support Singapore SMEs, to learn about overseas markets, land in those markets with business opportunities and localise their businesses for sustainable presence.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This has been positively received by enterprising SMEs which recognised the need to go beyond Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Janet Ang, if you can wrap up.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: So, the last point is: play the ecosystem game.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: What will be our competitive advantage and differentiator?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: Imagine green and sustainable Singapore-branded value chains where our Singapore SMEs, LLE, TLCs, MNCs and even Government-linked companies like PSA, Changi Airport, work together to innovate and transform our value chains for competitive advantage and deliver unique value.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: This would require research capability, IP assets, deep industry skills, broad cross-industry expertise and financial capital to create platforms for our company —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Janet Ang, you do need to wrap up.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: — to work together as a winning ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that in this year's Budget, a lot of additional resource is provided to bring about transformation of businesses, how do we ensure companies develop in line with the refreshed ITMs?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will the ITM refresh set clear direction on how to enhance our sustainability efforts, such as the use of sustainable aviation fuels, electric propulsion or hybrid propulsion, in the aerospace ITM refresh.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, a topic that never gets old is how we brace Singapore's economy for the future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To that end, the Government works closely with our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), industries and the Labour Movement to equip our workforce with the skills and knowledge which companies need.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The future is exciting with emerging, high-growth areas but it is also uncertain and dynamic with demand for workers and talent which is high.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We cannot guarantee what will happen in five or 10 years' time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In 2018, hardly anyone saw this pandemic slowing the airline industry to a halt, including the demand for manpower and local workers as well as retention.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, we need to build in flexibility as we train our workforce to be future-ready.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In providing continuous learning and training opportunities, perhaps we can model after our IHLs and structure courses that are more general, core modules that are applicable across groups of adjacent industries, together with specialised electives that are industry-specific and spend resources to reallocate talent with enhanced Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) by sector and using technology for skills matching.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How will Singapore ensure that firms, both present and future, continue to have access to the talent they need to support their expansion and operations in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, one of the key limiting factors going forward for us to achieve another economic growth trajectory is skill and knowledge-based manpower.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: I am concerned that our manpower policies use a macro approach without sufficient differentiation to help the whole economy transform.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: I am also concerned that our policies, such as salary threshold and dependency ratio ceilings, can only move in one direction every time they are reviewed, that is, further tightening.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Recovery or growth will be uneven across different sectors.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans can choose their jobs from different sectors of the economy.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: When a company wants to hire a Singaporean, it is competing with companies within its industry as well as with companies in other sectors.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: The larger, better capitalised companies in growth sectors have an advantage in drawing talent.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Take the example of digitalisation: when traditional sector companies want to go into digitalisation, they will need relevant IT professionals.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: However, with the growth of the tech sector in Singapore, IT professionals are in short supply.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore has become an important technology hub today and draws tech companies to headquarter and expand their activities here.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: This is the result of many years of building up the infrastructure and ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: We should support the tech sector's growth to its fullest.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: However, as the tech sector grows rapidly, it will hollow out relevant manpower from other sectors.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: This applies not just to IT professionals but also finance, marketing and compliance ones.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Companies in more traditional sectors may not be able to compete for the limited pool of Singapore talent in terms of pay or prospects.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Without the relevant IT professionals, these companies may have to slow down and suspend their transformation or digitalisation plans.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: This, in turn, will make them even less competitive.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Providing funding and technological support is useful, but to do the work, companies still need the warm bodies and brains.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: The cost of the manpower must also be sustainable for these companies.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, can I take my two cuts together?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: In Budget 2022, Minister Lawrence Wong highlighted that we have a window of opportunity for us to invest in building new capabilities to establish leading positions in key market segments.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: What are the growth and emerging sectors and how can companies seize opportunities in these sectors?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The pandemic has also heightened the need for companies to digitalise and accelerate the pace of adoption of digital and technology solutions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The current pandemic has shown that businesses that had invested and adapted digitally were more prepared for the disruptions and changes in operations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: What investments has the Government made and will make to encourage and groom Singapore companies, especially SMEs, to transform and adopt digital or tech solutions to be competitive?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: And what support will the Government provide to firms to do so?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Helping companies grow outside of Singapore has been a strategy for many decades.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: In recent years, with the disruptions, market shifts and, most recently, the pandemic, businesses do need to build new capabilities to compete globally.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Increasingly, the market opportunities are across sectors and industries.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: When companies venture overseas, apart from access to new markets, market insights and regulations, businesses require access to capital, supply chains and talent.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Against this changing landscape, how will local enterprises be supported to grow and build capabilities to compete globally?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: How will we foster stronger partnerships between MNCs and SMEs to help our enterprises collectively seize new opportunities in the global economy?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The Local Enterprises Funding Platform was part of last year’s Budget.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The objective was to help selected large Singapore firms transform and expand internationally.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: How is this different from the Local Enterprises Funding Platform?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Shawn Huang, take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: On enterprise development, over the years, the Government has provided much financial and non-financial support to SMEs.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As such, to better assist our SMEs to better access the assistance provided by the Government, how can Government schemes be streamlined so that they are more accessible to businesses, especially SMEs?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Our heartland enterprises are the heartbeat of our community.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: For decades, our heartland enterprises remain relevant as they provide us with much-needed daily essentials – fresh food as well as important services, such as hairdressing.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: However, digitalisation and e-commerce have changed the landscape substantially.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This is made more difficult as last-mile delivery becomes more common and affordable.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Our heartland enterprises have limited resources to keep up with digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As such, how can we support heartland enterprises to digitalise and build new capabilities?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: For manpower and talent: as the world is experiencing a wave of digitalisation, deep tech and scientific advancements, there is a global competition for talent.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The ability of companies and Singapore to compete globally is highly dependent on the amount of talent Singapore is able to access.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This is highly dependent on our Singapore workforce as well.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Our workforce must be relevant and have the skills to face the challenges of today and the future.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This is only possible if we continue to be diligent in maintaining our skills and update our knowledge and professional capabilities with the latest technologies, solutions and processes.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This requires a concerted effort on all fronts and in different phases of our manpower and talent development.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How will Singapore ensure that firms here continue to have access to talent they need to support their expansion and operations?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: What is the Government doing to build a future-ready workforce?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How is the Government supporting SMEs to improve the training and upskilling of local workers so that they stay relevant and competitive?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: On economic recovery, Mr Chairman, I would like to declare my interest as adviser to SIA's Staff Union (SIASU).

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Our local tourism industry is far from recovery levels.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Many working in the tourism sector continue to face many challenges, with reduced incomes and much uncertainty in the months ahead.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: An annual Business Survey conducted by Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) showed that a majority of Singapore companies, mostly SMEs, view rising costs, availability of suitable manpower, adaptation to COVID-19 safe management measures and transforming or pivoting to growth areas as top business challenges.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: MAS worked with financial institutions in Singapore to offer options for SMEs in need, to lower their short-term repayment obligations for their loans and to stay insured, despite facing financial difficulties.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Government has in place a suite of measures to support business transformation and help companies upskill and reskill their workforce, including the Enhanced Training Support for SMEs, that provides subsidies to sponsor employees to attend training courses funded by SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Businesses can also leverage the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to invest in their workforce development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Meanwhile, the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation supports leaders of promising SMEs in developing their capabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It has been a challenging period, but businesses are looking to find new opportunities to transform and grow.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: While the overall economy has grown significantly in 2021, we know that the growth has been uneven.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In particular, consumer-facing sectors, such as retail trade and Food and Beverage services, continue to face challenges due to the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: These SMEs provide important services to the community and hire large numbers of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How will the Government support SMEs overall, and specifically, in sectors with more challenging business conditions?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Besides providing the grants and assistance schemes, we would also need to make sure SMEs are aware of the support that is available to them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: While we acknowledge the many new or enhanced schemes and targeted support that have been rolled out in the last couple of years, SMEs may be overwhelmed by the information out there and unsure which schemes they are eligible for.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How would SMEs be able to find out more about the support that is available and access such support?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, our economy remains vital to Singaporeans’ livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There are four key areas that I would like to focus on: one, the progress of the Fair Tenancy Code of Conduct; two, our Business Hub status; three, opportunities and support for our businesses in our region post-COVID-19; and four, deepening our ecosystem and collaboration amongst MNCs and local companies.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While Singapore’s economic recovery has been led by trade-related and manufacturing sectors, this does not fully reflect all sectors and there are still sectors that continue to operate below pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This uneven recovery amongst businesses can potentially lead to wage disparities.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Consumer facing businesses continue to feel the prolonged impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Added to this, COVID-19 has also highlighted structural issues faced by consumer facing businesses.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A notable structural challenge is one of tenancies.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As many operate in spaces by way of tenancies, an unbalanced relationship and onerous tenancy conditions have exacerbated challenges faced by SMEs.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, there are four questions that I would like to raise pertaining to the Fair Tenancy Code of Conduct.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, what are the challenges and feedback received by the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Third, is MTI reviewing any parts of the code of conduct after gathering feedback and if so, which parts are under review?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To support businesses and jobs, Singapore must continue to function as a business hub.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We must continue to strive hard and be on the lookout for opportunities so that Singapore remains relevant to the global economy.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, with increased protectionism, competition from other global cities and travel restrictions, there is a need for the Singapore economy to build on our resilience and capability to catch the eye of opportunity providers.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, how has Singapore’s performance been as an investment destination amidst the COVID-19 pandemic?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, how can Singapore better distinguish itself as a more favourable business hub and enhance our competitiveness, especially in a post-BEPS 2.0 world?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What are the anticipated headwinds for Singapore and how are we positioning ourselves?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Asia’s economy continues to be of great value to Singapore and likewise, there is great potential from emerging markets which we can tap.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As a global Asia node, how is Singapore supporting our firms to capture opportunities in these markets and how has the support differed, compared to pre-COVID-19 times when the situation was different?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Also, what is MTI's assessment of our regional economies, especially the rise in public and household debts due to COVID-19, and how should our businesses, especially consumer facing businesses, account for these growth plans?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What are the concrete steps that Singapore is taking to strengthen our overall trade, economic and digital linkages with other relevant economic partners?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The various support grants that MTI has provided for enterprises, such as the Enterprise Development Grant have been timely to support local enterprises in their transformation.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In addition to developmental grants, how do we foster stronger partnerships with MNCs and SMEs to help our enterprises collectively seize new opportunities in the global economy that is increasingly competitive?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What are the strategies to deepen our ecosystem of businesses and collaborations to provide Singapore a competitive advantage in the global economy?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Lastly, how can we translate these strategies into increased productivity in SMEs as they face manpower and cash flow challenges?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Overall, as Singapore continues to recover and build new engines of growth, we must ensure that we exit this pandemic with an inclusive recovery in all sectors and industries.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to the roles the Minister had mentioned, I would like to make the following suggestions as to what more they can do and how MTI could support them.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This includes legal, accounting and human resource services, but also consultancy in core capabilities and internationalisation.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Second, TACs could be harnessed to administer appropriate Government schemes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The sectoral TACs can similarly take charge of sector-specific schemes, within parameters worked out jointly with the relevant Government body and with funding to support the costs incurred in administering the said programmes.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The TACs' closeness with their industry’s companies will be useful in that it is easier for them to explain how each scheme works and increase these companies’ participation in beneficial programmes and grants.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Third, regulatory authorities can consider devolving some regulatory functions to TACs, where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Such devolution is most easily achieved with professional certifications and if we push the envelope a bit more, even licensing.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: For example, instead of regulating the facilities management sector, the Building and Construction Authority has worked closely with the Singapore International Facilities Management Association to establish accreditation schemes for firms and facility management professionals.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, as debated in Parliament last year, my own association administers the Security Consultants Accreditation Programme.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: This, Sir, is a very excellent resource and reference document for TACs that can help them chart their development.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: On a related note, while TACs may get some funding from the Government pursuant to the LEAD grant, it should be the aim of all TACs to not only grow their operations and the services they offer to their members, but also to make sure they have the financial wherewithal to stand on their own two feet.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: On the strengthening of TACs to help SMEs, even as the Government has catered for significant resources to help SMEs in our pursuit of a digital and green economy, SMEs still see transformation as a cost, rather than a strategic investment or advantage.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Intensifying outreach to proactively engage SMEs was a point that Minister Gan Kim Yong made in his speech at the Budget debate recently.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: To accelerate our SMEs' growth in the new economy, there is room to do more to spark that mindset shift and marshal them towards the right resources, shape role models in different industries and to sustain partnerships in their transformational journey.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: In these aspects, I believe that the trade associations and chambers of commerce (TACs) can step up to play a bigger role and better define a role in partnering the Government.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: With their extensive networks, TACs can be an effective bridge between agencies and our businesses and are able to galvanise members as agents of change.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: In the next cut on measures to further support SMEs, Mr Chairman, the economic improvement in Singapore in 2021 is a testament to both the effectiveness of the Government's support measures for our SMEs, as well as the resilience of our local businesses.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Although we are not yet out of the woods in this pandemic, our SMES can be cautiously optimistic as the world progressively opens up.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: That said, there are concerns, given significant economic headwinds.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Higher energy prices and supply chain disruption continue to push business costs up.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Locally, our tighter wage policies relating to foreign labour have been structured to help our local workers and can also, therefore, translate into higher expenses for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: The recent crisis in Ukraine has compounded these worries, as it has exacerbated the rise in energy cost.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Oil prices are now expected to stay way higher than US$100 a barrel and business prospects looks a lot cloudier, when it looked a lot brighter, just a few weeks ago.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Against the backdrop of a prolonged energy crisis worsened by the Ukraine situation, which is still unfolding, will the Government consider further extending TRECS beyond May?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Beyond navigating higher business costs with funding support, the Government can also consider boosting non-financial measures to help our SMEs recover and grow.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: More than handouts, SMEs are eager for opportunities to get back on their feet.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Dylan Sharma, Vice President of the Singapore Association of Convention and Exhibition Organisers and Suppliers, or SACEOS, told me about pivots that MICE SMEs took and described that online became their lifeline.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While the industry deeply appreciates the Government's support schemes that enabled many to stay afloat, the association has given feedback that the demand aggregation (DA) procurement mechanism used by VITAL to improve Government procurement efficiency has locked out SMEs even though Mr Sharma himself and his company are on the panel.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Those who are not on the panel of vendors, he describes, are unable to compete for Government jobs for the few years related to the DA contract.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: On this note, what other non-financial measures can MTI further implement to support SMEs in their recovery?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Chairman, digitalisation is an imperative for SMEs to thrive in our new economy.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Nonetheless, I mentioned in my Budget speech that what weighs on the minds of SME owners is the certainty of cost increases against the uncertainty of the benefits related to digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While the Government has embarked on the journey to provide a nurturing ecosystem for SMEs to digitalise, there are still inertia and doubts that deter SMEs from taking that first step.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: I recently spoke with Mr Jimmy Goh, the owner of an SME 500 Awardee Sin Chwee Mini Mart who successfully digitalised his father's 30-year-old traditional seafood business with the help of an SME Centre.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: His feedback was about the heavy reliance on outsourced solution providers, noting that SMEs owners like him are not technologically savvy and have to go through a lot of trial and error.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: SMEs, therefore, worry about potentially getting locked into contracts and losing control of key business data as well as IT systems.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: How can MTI provide better assurance to SMEs with such concerns?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: The Association of Trade and Commerce also fed back that some SMEs feel that support can be a lot more holistic because, as beginners, they may not be clear of the holistic roadmap for a successful digitalisation, such as the need for online marketing after developing a sales channel.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: SMEs hence found themselves underestimating the costs and time required to build a digital channel.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: On this note, how can MTI provide more comprehensive support for SMEs to digitalise?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Chairman, digitalisation and innovation are no longer just the mainstays of larger companies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They are essential for any company to survive and thrive in the new economy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While larger companies have the expertise and resources to do so, SMEs find it much more challenging.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: SMEs also hire the bulk of our workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Thus, their growth is critical to the Singapore workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is even more so as the world becomes smaller and global competition ever closer to home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Budget 2022 focuses significantly on helping SMEs to boost their productivity by automating business processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There are two key challenges to adoption for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, talent is needed to digitalise and automate business processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With the escalating costs of talent acquisition, even eager SMEs might find their ambitions curtailed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In the longer run, having talent within the company allows for more robust implementation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How can the Ministry help to accelerate the training of such talent within companies?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In the interim, another option is to establish a common core of such talent that companies can buy services from.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Such consultancies are already commonplace but need to be amalgamated and subsidised for SMEs' adoption.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Despite the vastness and accessibility of information, identifying opportunities in the digital economy that suit the SMEs is even more difficult than ever.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Because of the exponential increase in opportunities and also threats, deciding on business opportunities is more complex than ever.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Companies suffer from either choice paralysis or analysis paralysis, or both.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One of the more common curation tools used to be trade visits or trade delegations to overseas markets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In this new digital economy, this will neither be necessary nor desired.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry share how they are helping our firms to identify new opportunities in the digital economy?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Digitalisation and innovation are complementary but distinct processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry share how we can support enterprises in reaping the benefits of R&D outcomes?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In the short run, support for enterprises to tap on the opportunities presented by digitalisation and innovation is crucial.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In the long run, we must seek to assist enterprises to grow their innovation capabilities independently to ensure continued R&D efforts even where Governmental support is not provided.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry share how it has been assisting our enterprises to grow their capabilities independently in the near future?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to first declare my interest as President of the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE).

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In my Budget Debate speech, I spoke at length about the choices that consumers can make to alleviate the rise in our cost of living.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But all our efforts will be in vain if we fail to clamp down on unscrupulous businesses which take advantage of the inflationary environment and engage in unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have three suggestions to strengthen the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act or CPFTA.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, we need to be able to take faster action against errant businesses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Under the current regulations, CASE may invite errant businesses to enter into a Voluntary Compliance Agreement (VCA) to cease its unfair practices and to compensate affected consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As the name suggests, such agreements are entered into on a voluntary basis and businesses which refuse the VCA are then referred to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) for investigation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This long lead time can lead to: one, a continuation of the unfair practices; or two, allow the errant business time to wind down their companies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: If unaddressed, this will severely undermine public confidence in our consumer protection regime.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Second, the Courts must be able to order errant businesses to compensate the affected consumers during an injunction application by CCCS.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Currently, even if CCCS successfully obtains an injunction order against an errant business, affected consumers are still required to separately file their cases at the Small Claims Tribunal to seek compensation and this can be an onerous process for some consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I propose to amend the CPFTA to provide the Courts with the discretion to compel errant businesses to compensate affected consumers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is already practised in countries such as Australia, and I believe that doing so will provide consumers with quicker financial relief.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Third, we should expand the ambit of regulated contracts under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) (Cancellation of Contracts) Regulations to include beauty-related contracts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Complaints against the beauty industry took the top spot in 2021, with many consumers complaining of pressure sales tactics and misleading claims.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Despite our best efforts, such unfair business practices continue to run rampant.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This allows consumers the necessary time and space to consider whether they truly want to go ahead with the purchase, especially those that involve large prepayment amounts.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Mr Chairman, how will the Committee Against Profiteering be implemented and how will it address concerns of businesses perceived to be profiteering from the GST increase?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can the committee identify the singular cause of price increase and hence, identify businesses profiteering from GST in light of increasing costs of supplies, rental, labour, energy, in addition to the stepped increases in GST?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can we ensure the committee is effective in protecting our residents?

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Chairman, we are now in the third year of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our enterprises and our workers have shown tremendous resilience, particularly our frontline workers and our healthcare workers, amidst a challenging and constantly evolving environment.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our strong economic fundamentals, such as our excellent infrastructure, our vibrant innovation ecosystem, our extensive connectivity to the region and the world, and our trusted and robust regulatory environment, also provided us the ballast to ride out the storm.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These projects are expected to create more than 17,300 jobs and close to $17 billion in value-added per annum.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Median real income grew by 0.9% after accounting for inflation and our resident unemployment rate has come down to 3.2%, which is close to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Government has leaned forward to provide generous support to help enterprises through the past two years.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We recognise that the recovery has been uneven across sectors and we will continue to extend assistance in a targeted manner.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He also announced an extension of various loan schemes administered by Enterprise Singapore, to facilitate access to financing for Small and Medium Enterprises, or SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also do more to give the tourism industry a further lift, as we prepare for international travel to return eventually.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling will provide more details in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am heartened that many of our enterprises do not want to just sit on their hands and wait for the pandemic to pass.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, they want to make full use of this time-out period, to uplift themselves and their workers, so that they are ready to sprint ahead when the pandemic subsides.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Transformation will become even more important in the years ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Edward Chia asked about the economic headwinds we may face in the coming years and what we are doing to enhance Singapore's competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our external environment is increasingly volatile and uncertain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Pandemics and extreme weather conditions are becoming more common.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Technology and business cycles are shortening and changes in international economic regulations, such as the impending BEPS 2.0, will affect how we attract and anchor investments here.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Geopolitical shifts, big power contestation and rising protectionism are also underway.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The ongoing crisis in Ukraine is yet another reminder that peace and security, the foundation for economic growth, cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a small and open economy, we cannot insulate ourselves from these external factors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will need to muster the agility and fortitude to adapt and stay ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As Ms Mariam Jaafar said in her speech, we must work hard to secure our position as a stable and trusted global business hub, which includes steadily reopening our borders, committing to a strategy of COVID-19 resilience and welcoming investments, ideas and people from all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I know many are concerned about how doing business is getting more expensive and costly, as Mr Liang Eng Hwa pointed out.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Minister for Finance in his round up speech explained what the Government is doing to support businesses and assured the House that we will monitor the situation closely and step up our support if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While there are headwinds, there are also many exciting developments in key sectors across our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To position ourselves for growth and seize these opportunities, we must continue to invest in our fundamentals and build up strong capabilities in our enterprises and our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have already started on this important work.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Future Economy Council is refreshing all 23 Industry Transformation Maps, or ITMs, to refine our transformation strategy up to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Sharael Taha, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Pritam Singh asked about the progress of the ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are currently working closely with industry stakeholders, unions and academia to update our ITMs, to address emerging trends and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include digitalisation, resilience and as Mr Sharael Taha suggested, sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Jobs and skills, including the upskilling of workers, is also a key thrust of ITM 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Precision Engineering ITM aimed to add 3,000 PMET jobs from 2015 to 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The sector is doing well and as of 2019, the number of PMET jobs in the sector has already increased by about 4,000.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The ongoing ITM Refresh seeks to enable the sector to capitalise on digital manufacturing and create good jobs in growth areas such as additive manufacturing and robotics.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The other ITM 2025 reviews are also in progress and will take into account the outcomes achieved from the earlier round of ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked about growth and emerging opportunities and business sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For the longer term, we need a collective vision for the economy – the Singapore Economy 2030 vision – which will outline our ambition, provide direction and coordinate actions across key pillars of our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Together, these efforts will put our industries, enterprises and workers on a firmer footing for long-term, sustainable growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Singapore has a large and diversified services sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It represents more than 70% of our economy, comprising industries such as finance and insurance, information and communications, professional services and logistics.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The bulk of our services sector is export-oriented and has shown remarkable resilience through the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Looking ahead, there are two major waves of opportunities – sustainability and digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I will speak more on sustainability and our Green Economy Strategy, as part of the Joint Segment on the Singapore Green Plan, next week.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Digitalisation is a secular trend which will disrupt all our industries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence and machine learning, as well as augmented and virtual reality, have the potential to fundamentally transform how we interact with the world around us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As more companies accelerate investments in digitalisation, there will also be increased demand for services such as consultancy and marketing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, as businesses move online, companies will need the expertise of marketing services firms to create more personalised advertising campaigns with the use of data analytics and marketing technology, or "martech" tools, and to engage customers through immersive user experiences through gamification, and augmented and virtual reality.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Firms will also need to build new capabilities through collaborating with partners from other industries to co-create multidisciplinary solutions, including in areas such as logistics.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am glad to see many homegrown companies leveraging global opportunities afforded by the digital economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of you would have heard of Nium, a Singapore-based fintech unicorn that builds white label cross-border payment solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, its software is getting money to people and businesses in over 190 markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another example is AP Media, a Singapore marketing firm that specialises in interactive and video content production.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the height of the pandemic, AP Media developed a livestreaming and virtual conference tool which was used for Singapore's first virtual fashion show called "The Front Row".

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The online portal houses a 3D arena, which visitors can virtually navigate runway shows, panels, workshops and podcasts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: AP Media's creative technology has since been deployed in several international projects, notably Louis Vuitton's fashion show and Razer's Global Virtual Conference.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Digitalisation can also be a powerful transformation tool to help consumer-facing businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They help them improve productivity and to engage new customers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Singapore houses Sephora's Digital Centre of Excellence in areas such as marketing, creative and design and data analysis.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One of the solutions it created in-house here in Singapore is the Virtual Artist Kiosk, which relies on augmented reality to reflect the various lipstick colours on their consumers through a digital screen.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Real-time analytics, such as user engagement and the popularity of products, are then channelled back to Sephora's platform.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second Minister Tan See Leng will speak more about what we are doing to help firms seize opportunities in digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we invest in our services ecosystem, we will continue to build up a strong manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Thanks to our continued investments over the years, we have a thriving and competitive manufacturing ecosystem which exports products all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are also a major player in the biomedical industry and pharmaceutical companies have been producing lifesaving drugs from Singapore to supply to global markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: GE Aviation Engine Services Singapore, which I visited last year, recently became the first maintenance repair and overhaul (MRO) facility in the world to use advanced additive manufacturing technology to repair airfoil components in commercial jet engines.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will further entrench its position as GE Aviation's largest site globally for engine component MRO and strengthen Singapore's aerospace industry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Advanced manufacturing in food-related value chains also offers exciting growth opportunities, especially in areas with strong synergy with sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Oatside is one such local plant-based startup and Singapore's first homegrown oat milk brand.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It focuses on sustainable sourcing and production and is tapping on Enterprise Singapore's Market Readiness Assistance grant to gear up for expansion in Southeast Asia, Korea, Japan, China and the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I thought Members would be excited to try this local product, so I have arranged for Oatside milk to be served in the dining areas here at Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: You can try the milk on its own or have it with some freshly made coffee from Hook Coffee, a local coffee company that has expanded significantly through leveraging e-commerce.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our economic agencies will provide bespoke support for manufacturers with strong potential, to deepen their capabilities and expand their global reach.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example of a globally oriented Singapore manufacturer is Akribis Systems, a global leader in motion control solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Akribis owns core technologies in direct drive motor components, robotic actuators and linear stages which are critical to build high precision equipment for the semiconductor, electronics and medtech industries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Akribis is headquartered in Singapore and has a factory and innovation centre here.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It has significant global reach, with its overseas businesses contributing to over 75% of its total revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must continue to strengthen Singaporeans' interest in manufacturing and develop a strong local pipeline of talent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also need to ensure that Singaporeans can access the good job opportunities in the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To level up the industry's talent development capabilities, the Singapore Precision Engineering and Technology Association (SPETA) will work with industry partners such as the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association and our Institutes of Higher Learning to develop a Manufacturing Employer Handbook.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Handbook will provide a range of human capital best practices and resources, to support companies in developing structured career development and progression pathways for their employees.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: SPETA will identify and work with at least 20 companies to pilot the adoption of these practices and pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These internships can go a long way in shaping students' perception of the sector and kindle their interest.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example is KABAM Robotics, a robotics solution provider headquartered in Singapore in the service robotics industry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: KABAM currently has three interns in roles such as software and hardware development and is looking to bring on another five soon.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One of its past interns, Ms Rachel Lim from the Temasek Polytechnic School of Engineering, was given the opportunity to work in the Products team to support the design, development and assembly of robots, as well as conduct performance testing and analysis.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Rachel enjoyed her stint so much that she has decided to join KABAM as a full-time Product Engineer starting next week.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will support companies to hire and train ITE graduates for critical technician and assistant engineer roles through on-the-job training, with career progression pathways and competitive salaries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Given our small domestic market, global connectivity is essential to help our enterprises grow beyond our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As one of the world's leading business and transport hubs located in one of the most economically dynamic part of the world, we are in a very strong position to take advantage of growth opportunities in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked how we will secure Singapore's status as a key node in the global trading network.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Edward Chia also asked how we are helping our companies seize regional opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are embarking on a few key moves.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, we are proactively strengthening regional economic integration through ASEAN and other platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is particularly important in a bifurcated world with increased protectionism and global competition.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Greater regional cooperation and integration will not only enhance access to markets and create opportunities for our businesses, but also enlarge the economic pie for our entire region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are playing a leading role in key regional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), such as the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, or RCEP, which is the world's largest FTA, and as the Chair of the Commission of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, or CPTPP, this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also continue to facilitate trade by shaping the rules of the game and setting high standards in emerging areas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are pioneering new agreements, such as Digital Agreements, which facilitate cross-border data flows and digital trade, as well as Green Economy Agreements.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work with like-minded partners such as UK, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and others, to secure benefits for our companies and our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is important to help our enterprises, especially the SMEs, utilise and benefit from FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Singapore's network of 27 FTAs has brought many benefits to our companies, including tariff savings, stronger intellectual property and investment protection, a more conducive business environment and increased regulatory transparency.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to work with industry partners, including the Singapore Business Federation, to proactively engage SMEs and provide them with the necessary support to take advantage of our FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also want to capture more re-exports and transshipment flows, to embed Singapore more deeply into the global supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To achieve this ambition, we need to redouble our efforts to build a strong ecosystem in trading companies and activities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will boost our efforts to attract leading Global Traders and increase value capture for Singapore by anchoring more of their upstream, downstream and innovation activities here.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These Global Traders will also serve as platforms to help other Singapore companies to break into overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also accelerate efforts to grow a strong core of Singapore Global Traders, which are locally grown traders that command global scale and are highly innovative.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To do so, Enterprise Singapore will tap on its full range of programme offerings, such as Scale-up SG and the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation Programme, and provide bespoke support tailored to each firm's unique circumstances and ambitions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These will cover areas such as talent development, innovation, internationalisation and financing.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For instance, Fish International Sourcing House (FISH), is a homegrown seafood trader and graduate of the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It has established presence in over 90 markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To grow its trading business further, the company plans to invest more than $20 million to set up a 240,000-square feet seafood processing and innovation centre in Singapore, which will enable it to seize new growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, FISH intends to almost triple its current headcount of 25 by hiring another 45 employees over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: FISH is also poised to have an impact on our larger trading ecosystem by partnering Singapore enterprises and helping them break into new markets, by allowing them to leverage its existing strong overseas distribution network to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Growing our trading volume will create good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To take on the many attractive opportunities that will emerge from the continued growth of this sector, we must build a workforce with skills and knowledge needed.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have embarked on a suite of workforce upgrading initiatives for the trade sector, such as the creation of a Jobs Transformation Map and a Career Conversion Programme for Wholesale Trade Professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, we are working with industry and the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to develop more talent in the trading of commodities such as Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) and carbon credits.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our Singapore Economy 2030 vision needs to be supported by a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises that are future-ready, globally competitive and possess deep innovative capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second Minister Tan See Leng will elaborate on the concrete steps that we will be taking.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our Singapore Economy 2030 vision would be neither achievable nor meaningful, if it is not anchored on an unwavering belief in uplifting our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Enterprises also need a strong workforce with the right skillsets and capabilities to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how the Government is building a future-ready workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
