text: This must be a whole-of-economy effort with close coordination and collaboration between workers, companies and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Minister for Education Mr Chan Chun Sing and Minister for Manpower Dr Tan See Leng will be elaborating on initiatives to develop our local workforce, and help displaced workers upskill and reskill, so that they can continue to fulfil their potential by taking on new job roles or moving to emerging sectors in a nimble fashion.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Ms Janet Ang that company-led training (CLT) is critical.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Companies need to step up, to consistently and persistently invest in human capital to recruit, retain and nurture talent.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Workers too need to play their part and be open to learning new skills and adapting to new roles.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the Minister for Finance announced in the Budget speech, we have relaxed the eligibility criteria for the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit (SFEC) for one year, to enable more small and microenterprises to tap on the credits and upskill their workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There is simply no substitute for well-structured on-the-job training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Besides ensuring that workers are trained in relevant skills, such investments by employers can also help create a highly engaged and productive workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I agree with Ms Foo Mee Har that initiatives like the Company Training Committees, or CTCs, play an important role in this regard.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NTUC Deputy Secretary-General Chee Hong Tat had earlier spoken at length about how CTCs have supported companies in their transformation efforts during the Budget debate.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example is Vicinity Studio, a local content production company founded in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This helped Vicinity take steps to improve its HR capabilities and staff competencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I urge enterprises to tap on these available resources and work with us to strengthen our economy and workers together.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our enterprises and workers have come far in the fight against the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The pandemic is not yet over, and the future will continue to surprise us and challenge us in more ways than one.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The chapters of our Economy 2030 vision are filled with exciting stories waiting to be written.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As we continue our work to grow and develop our economy, we can look forward to a wide spectrum of new career and business opportunities for our workers and enterprises to explore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some of these may not even exist today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As long as we continue to stand together as one, as we have done through the pandemic, and look upon the future with a spirit of enterprise and discovery, I have every confidence that we will make progress towards building a future economy that will meet the aspirations of our workers and companies, and inspire generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our local enterprises are a critical part of Singapore's growth story.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They account for almost 70% of jobs in Singapore and have the potential to help us venture into new growth areas, create solutions for the world and reimagine Singapore's economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Riding on global economic recovery last year, we registered a strong economic performance and we had projected GDP growth of 3% to 5% for 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Minister Gan has earlier shared in this House that it is still too early to estimate the actual impact on Singapore's economic growth this year, given the conflict in Ukraine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The situation is fast evolving and there will be greater uncertainties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In an increasingly volatile environment, the only way to navigate these challenges is to strengthen our resilience and accelerate our transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Despite the pandemic, many of our local enterprises have not sat still.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They have pressed on with transformation and they are now in a stronger position to rebound and capture growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They have sought to turn the crisis into an opportunity of a generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is the spirit that will power the Enterprise 2030 strategy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Janet Ang asked how we are supporting our local enterprises to grow and compete globally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Enterprise 2030 strategy is our response to ensure that we build and sustain a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises that are future-ready and possess deep capabilities to compete globally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, we must support the growth of high potential companies to become global champions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, we will strengthen the core capabilities of the broader base of local enterprises in industry transformation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Over the last few years, we have witnessed the emergence of a new generation of local champions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We now have 22 homegrown startups that have reached unicorn status.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many of our homegrown companies such as Secretlab, Hegen and Nanofilm, have made a name for themselves internationally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are the bright spots in our enterprise landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will intensify our efforts to identify, nurture and to grow many more promising local enterprises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Both ESG and EDB will provide more bespoke and enterprise-centric assistance to enterprises with strong growth potential and global ambitions which are tailored to their specific needs and individual growth ambitions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also harness resources across whole-of-Government and our partners to support each of these high potential enterprises in areas such as innovation, internationalisation and fostering partnerships with other firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For a start, we will enhance our support for these high potential companies in four ways: firstly, developing global-ready executives; secondly, creating new corporate ventures; thirdly, facilitating Mergers and Acquisitions; and fourthly, creating enhanced access to financing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how we will continue to ensure that firms have access to the talent they need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also been exploring new ways to support companies in creating new business ventures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last year, EDB launched the Corporate Venture Launchpad, which is a pilot programme to support companies to incubate and launch new businesses within a six-month sprint.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As part of this programme, Keppel Land is venturing into digital well-being, companion care and connectivity solutions for eldercare, in line with its ambition to become a leading player in the Senior Living sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Given the positive feedback from the pilot programme, we will expand the Corporate Venture Launchpad to support a wider range of companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We know that it takes courage, it takes gumption to scale a business.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These funds are the Local Enterprises Fund @ 65 and the Anchor Fund @ 65 which are set up in partnership with Temasek, as well as the Growth IPO Fund managed by EDBI.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked about the progress of the Local Enterprises Fund. 65 Equity Partners, a wholly owned investment platform of Temasek, has been managing this fund and engaging promising local enterprises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have seen good interest in the fund since its launch.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But these are still early days and many of these plans will take time and a certain runway to finalise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will step up efforts to help the broad base of SMEs in four key areas: one, capabilities development; two, internationalisation; three, digitalisation; and four, innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have rolled out a comprehensive suite of programmes to support our enterprises and workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Edward Chia and Ms Janet Ang asked how the Government will foster stronger partnerships between MNCs or Large Local Enterprises (LLEs) and SMEs to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will work with SkillsFuture Singapore to onboard MNCs and large local enterprises who are "Queen Bees" to curate industry-relevant training courses in emerging growth areas, such as robotics and Industry 4.0.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Under this scheme, we have supported collaborations between large companies and smaller SMEs through co-innovation, internationalisation projects as well as costs of supplier qualification processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies can qualify up to 70% for manpower and consultancy costs and up to 50% for hardware and equipment costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I strongly urge interested enterprises to get in touch with our agencies for more details.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have been working with many LLEs to do so and we will adopt a more concerted "Team Singapore" approach in our internationalisation strategy and bring onboard SMEs to collectively access overseas markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I am encouraged that 1,600 local enterprises embarked on internationalisation projects last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is in spite of current travel restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many of these enterprises have gained a foothold in key markets through our support networks such as the GlobalConnect@SBF, as well as leveraged on ESG's international matchmaking platforms, such as the Open Innovation Network to connect and co-innovate with other industry players.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will intensify efforts through these international partnerships and networks to help SMEs deepen their presence in key markets and pursue opportunities in new ones.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Desmond Choo asked how we are helping firms to digitalise, strengthen capabilities and capture new opportunities in the digital economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One way we are doing so is through the SMEs Go Digital initiative, which supports SMEs in the adoption of digital solutions for basic business functions, online transactions and other more advanced solutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, firms can also tap on funding support from ESG's Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) and Enterprise Development Grant (EDG).

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As announced in the Budget Speech, we will expand the range of solutions under the PSG, to include new technologies and more sector-specific solutions to deepen capabilities in areas, such as cybersecurity and data analytics, which will increasingly become essential skillsets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: On Mr Desmond Choo's suggestion to help SMEs tap on a pool of tech talent, this is exactly why IMDA has launched the Chief Technology Officer-as-a-Service (CTO-as-a-Service) scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the name suggests, SMEs can engage a pool of digital consultants for in-depth advisory and project management services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MCI will share more on the digitalisation initiatives later on, today, at the Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also study Ms Foo Mee Har's suggestion to replicate the CTO-as-a-service scheme to other functions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: On Mr Derrick Goh's point to provide more holistic support for companies, I want to highlight that the schemes I mentioned earlier are part of a comprehensive suite of tools to support our enterprises in each stage of their growth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, more can be done to raise awareness and help our SMEs understand how the various tools can support their needs, as mentioned by both Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Mr Shawn Huang.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I encourage enterprises to reach out to Enterprise Singapore and our network of SME Centres for free one-on-one business advisory.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how the Government is supporting enterprises in their innovation and R&D journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Over the years, we have taken a more enterprise-centric approach to help SMEs build their innovation capabilities and translate their innovations into new products and services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since 2003, more than 950 A*STAR research scientists and engineers have been seconded to support over 850 local SMEs in product development as part of A*STAR's Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading programme, or T-UP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ESG has also enhanced its Innovation Advisors Programme to partner industry veterans with SMEs to commercialise their research.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are significant efforts to help our SMEs scale up their capabilities in-house.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also reaped the fruits of our labour.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Fortitude kits have been deployed in Singapore and more than 40 countries globally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Apart from COVID-19-related innovations, we are also encouraged to see more local firms innovating and moving up the value chain.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I visited another local startup, ION Mobility, last year to unveil its flagship product, the ION Mobius.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is a smart electric motorbike which was conceptualised, designed and assembled in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, its proprietary battery pack allows riders to cover a distance of up to 200 kilometres on a single charge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And its interface settings can also be changed with the rider's smartphone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have invested substantial resources and efforts in building innovation capabilities, and I agree with Mr Desmond Choo that, beyond Government support, importantly, our enterprises must also embrace the spirit of innovation as a core capability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I am excited to see how our enterprises will push the boundaries to create solutions for the world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: After having set out our longer term plans, I would like to address some of our near-term challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Minister for Finance and Minister for Trade and Industry have touched on many of these issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on our energy supply.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Derrick Goh also asked how we are supporting consumers due to rising energy prices and whether these measures could be extended.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, I would like to assure all consumers that we will spare no effort to ensure that Singapore's energy supply remains secure and reliable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I understand the cost pressures faced by households and businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to monitor market developments and will not hesitate to introduce further measures, if necessary, to support vulnerable consumers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Eligible households will continue to receive U-Save rebates to support them with their utility expenses and businesses which need financing support can tap on the loans offered by ESG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I agree with Mr Liang Eng Hwa that we can enhance energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, we have rolled out a series of measures to encourage consumers to do so by redesigning electricity bills to benchmark individual consumption across other similar users and mandating energy-intensive companies to implement energy conservation and energy management practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, we cannot embark and succeed on this journey alone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We urge all consumers to use energy prudently and adopt energy conservation as a way of life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are pressing ahead with our efforts to advance the energy transition and decarbonise the power sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will elaborate more on this in the Joint Segment on the Singapore Green Plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Domestically, the labour market in Singapore has tightened over the past year due to economic recovery and international border restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many businesses continued to find it challenging to access the manpower they require, especially in areas where there are skill shortages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Saktiandi Supaat pointed out, access to highly-skilled manpower is a critical challenge we must overcome together, given our ageing population, economic uncertainties and the competition for global talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Therefore, we have made various adjustments to our foreign worker policies to be more targeted and selective in bringing in high-quality and diverse foreign workforce to complement the local workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao asked whether our foreign workforce policies are dynamic and flexible enough to meet our economic needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to actively monitor and review these schemes to ensure that they are effective.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will also share more on the refinements to address skill shortages later on this afternoon at MOM's COS debate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In Mandarin):   We are committed to support our local enterprises to leverage growth opportunities in a post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond targeted measures to address immediate cost pressures and greater uncertainties brought by the conflict in Ukraine, we need to accelerate industry transformation efforts in the light of the larger transformation and restructuring of our global economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As part of our Enterprise 2030 strategy, we will encourage and support the growth of high potential companies to become global champions and strengthen the core capabilities of the broad base of SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In particular, we will intensify efforts in capability development and supporting internationalisation, digitalisation and innovation in our local SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will support our SMEs on this journey, so that we can seize opportunities, achieve breakthroughs and build a more resilient and vibrant economy together.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In English): We have set out our strategy under Enterprise 2030 which will allow us to set our sights further, plan for the longer term and put in place the building blocks right now.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, we have gone through two long and hard years since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Despite the challenging and uncertain business environment which upended lives and operations, Singapore enterprises have shown incredible resilience and mettle to transform and thrive in the new normal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As encouraged by Minister Gan Kim Yong and Second Minister Tan See Leng, we have the chance to seize the new opportunities that are before us and to forge a new path forward for our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will leave no stones unturned to enable our people and businesses to emerge even stronger than before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First and foremost, we know that access to financing is the lifeblood of business survival and growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To ensure that our enterprises have ready access to financing at various stages of their development, the Government has put in place a range of support measures specifically for this purpose.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As the Minister for Finance Mr Lawrence Wong recently announced in Budget 2022 just two weeks ago, we will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme (TBLP), as well as the enhanced EFS Project Loan (EFS-PL) and EFS Trade Loan (EFS-TL).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also be making further enhancements to schemes, such as the EFS Merger and Acquisition (M&A) scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These improvements come on the back of industry feedback and engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One company that has benefited from the EFS M&A scheme is GKE Corporation Ltd.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a third-party logistics provider that provides warehousing, freight services, transportation, marine logistics and port management services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They took up an EFS M&A loan of $6 million to fund the acquisition of a chemical tolling company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This strategic acquisition will help GKE acquire deeper technical expertise in specialty chemical manufacturing and capture a broader segment of customers as a market leader for chemical logistics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will provide fresh avenues of financing for the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) that was just launched last October has an Enterprise Financing Scheme component called EFS-Green, designed to help our local enterprises capture opportunities and develop capabilities in sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Sectors involving Clean Energy, Circular Economy, Green Infrastructure and Clean Transportation are well-placed to tap into this source of funding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These enhancements to keep the financing tap on will reassure Ms Rahayu Mahzam that companies can access the vital support they need to seize green shoots of opportunities and tide through the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to monitor the schemes' efficacy and fine-tune them to give our local companies our fullest support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Apart from financing, I would like to assure Mr Shawn Huang and Ms Rahayu Mahzam that our enterprises have a one-stop portal called GoBusiness to rely on for all the latest information and e-services for doing business in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, by answering a few simple questions on the portal, they can receive tailored recommendations from its e-Adviser feature – from the kind of Government grants suited for their transformation journey, to how to start and grow their business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage our companies, entrepreneurs and business owners to make full use of this business-friendly online resource.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On this note, I want to assure Mr Derrick Goh that while the Government aims to achieve greater efficiencies through technology and streamlining processes, we are also mindful of the need to ensure an inclusive playing field of opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hear his concerns that the use of the demand aggregation procurement by VITAL could limit opportunities for SMEs to be appointed on the Government's panel of suppliers and providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the demand aggregation tender involving the events management industry late last year, a decision was made after feedback from the industry, to structure the contract such that, in addition to lower financial barriers, smaller event management companies could have a chance to be appointed onto this panel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This also led to a doubling in the number of bids attracted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, I want to assure Mr Derrick Goh that, wherever it is appropriate, we aim to structure the procurement in such a way that a range of suppliers of different profiles and sizes can take part, so as to offer business opportunities for as many enterprises as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, COVID-19 has hit some sectors very hard and we will continue to avail support to those that need it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Edward Chia pointed out, consumer-facing businesses are bearing the prolonged impact of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the last two years, the food services and retail sectors have battled waves of disruptions time and time again, from restrictions to closures, to changing consumer preferences and also pressures to digitalise, as well as manpower shortages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the accelerated pace of change and the fast-emerging consumer trends, the food and retail sectors have to continue to transform themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to help them recover, we want to help them get stronger and we want to help them forge ahead with new strength.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This extension under the Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package will give our F&B and also our retail businesses more scope and more opportunities to adapt and transform and better position themselves for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since 2020, Dian Xiao Er – I think this is a name that some of us are familiar with – has tapped on the EDG for three projects to enhance their central kitchen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of the projects involves the development of a first-of-its-kind automated duck conveyor system, which then helps to cut the preparation time for 1,500 ducks by about one-third.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I note that it is 12.00 noon and for me to talk about 1,500 ducks, I think, is very tempting to the Members in the Chamber.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With less manual work that is required in the duck preparation process, Dian Xiao Er retrained their staff to take on other roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, by taking on duties in their manufacturing central kitchen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: By sharing this example, I hope that our food services and retail companies will make full use of the newly introduced $70 million Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package to enable more such companies like Dian Xiao Er to continue pursuing their business transformation efforts, so as to stay competitive and future-ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, we also recognise that manpower challenges continue to feature at the top of the food services and retail sectors' concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together with industry associations, such as the Restaurant Association of Singapore (RAS) and the Singapore Retailers' Association (SRA), we will double up on our efforts to support the hiring and training of local jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will include promoting local talent development programmes, such as the SGUnited Career Pathways scheme and the Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs), as well as intensifying our outreach to jobseekers and supporting the sectors' training needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am also pleased to update the House and Mr Edward Chia that all Government landlords and major private sector landlords have adopted the Code of Conduct for the Leasing of Retail Premises since 1 June 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We can look forward to updates to the Code from the FTIC, which is the Fair Tenancy Industry Committee, in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These updates will then provide us with additional clarity and details on the implementation of the Code as its legal enactment gets underway.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, our tourism sector keeps Singapore connected to the rest of the world and maintains our position as a global-Asia node.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: COVID-19 has hit the tourism sector very hard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: But despite the challenges, we have continued to quickly adapt and pivot to new propositions to come back even stronger.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to support our tourism sector's efforts to recover, innovate and to come back stronger than before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To answer Mr Shawn Huang's questions about our plans to support our tourism sector's recovery, allow me to share some of our strategies and plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, Singapore Tourism Board (STB) will accelerate its SingapoReimagine international recovery campaign, in tandem with the resumption of international travel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: STB is now working with a wide range of partners around the world, such as airlines, travel agents and media outlets, to maintain Singapore's position as a global-Asia node to attract more travellers here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will help tourism companies develop attractive new products and experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The SRV was part of a larger effort, which is the SingapoRediscovers campaign, which is still ongoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through this campaign, STB works with hotels, attractions and tour operators to create new products and experiences that appeal not only to Singaporeans but also to visitors when they return to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, the tour operator Let's Go Tour Singapore developed new and unique programmes in the course of the SRV scheme and, as a result, they enjoyed a three-fold jump in their revenue compared to pre-COVID-19 times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: STB will continue to engage and also support tourism companies so that Singapore will have a broader and richer range of unique experiences and products that differentiate us from other cities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, we will defend our position as a leading destination for high-quality business and leisure events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hit a "pause" button on these because of COVID-19, but STB is now gearing up to resume large-scale, and also, high-quality business and leisure events from this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Later this year, we will welcome many more industry-leading events, such as the Global Health Security Conference 2022, the FIND – Design Fair Asia 2022, as well as the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix and the Standard Chartered Singapore Marathon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These events will not only directly benefit the tourism sector but will also ensure that Singapore remains a "top of mind" destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Fourth, we will continue to co-curate innovative tech and digital solutions with the tourism sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the past three years, STB's Singapore Tourism Accelerator Programme supported 34 promising tech startups in developing solutions to future-proof the tourism industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of them is Bazaar and this is a local startup which offers augmented reality solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Bazaar developed gamified wayfinding solutions for Marina Bay Sands to enhance its customer engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And beyond the Accelerator Programme, Bazaar is now planning to tap on opportunities in the metaverse to support tourism businesses in developing immersive experiences for their customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Fifth, we will double down on efforts to upskill the tourism sector workforce to ensure that tourism workers are ready to meet changing job demands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This helped more than 1,300 workers take on redesigned and enhanced roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: STB has also set up the Tourism Careers Hub pilot jointly with NTUC and the five main travel Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to provide job facilitation, skills training and also, business transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, to complement the suite of support that the Government has directly rolled out to businesses, we will continue to work with partners, such as the TACs. on collective actions to transform and better position our industries for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As the eyes, ears and mouth for their members, TACs play an important role in the sectors that they represent and this was a point that was highlighted by many of the Members yesterday – Mr Raj Joshua Thomas, Ms Janet Ang and other Members as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am always of the view that the TACs' roles actually can be easily summarised by "ABC".

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Because "A", the TACs advocate their members' interests; "B", they help their members by bridging the communications between the members and the Government; and "C", they help their members by collaborating with others, including from other sectors to capture new opportunities for the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Two months ago, I attended the launch of the TAC Competency Framework and the TAC Growth Model.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I note that Mr Raj Joshua Thomas also highlighted this in his speech yesterday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Framework and Growth Model were developed by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) with the support of the Singapore Business Federation (SBF), the Enterprise Singapore (ESG) and the SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Eligible TACs can access a range of digital solutions and training courses that is curated to equip TAC staff with basic e-capabilities that will help raise their productivity and efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will support secretariat members and TAC leaders nominated by their TACs to attend the TAC Leadership Development Programme, so as to boost their leadership capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Thirdly, to boost the TAC talent pool, SBF will, with support from Enterprise Singapore and SCCCI, develop a TAC Leadership Accelerator Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This programme seeks to attract talented, high-performing mid-career professionals with industry-relevant experience to join our TACs and to take industry transformation efforts to a higher plane.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To become effective leaders in industry development, the candidates will undergo a mix of classroom training and mentorship programmes and also gain on-the-job experience in the participating TACs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am very heartened that SBF, as the apex business chamber, has stepped forward as an anchor and advocate for a stronger TAC community to help our businesses grow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More details on the new programmes will be made available this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, in the area of partnerships with the industry, MTI is working closely with the different industry representatives to form the Committee Against Profiteering (CAP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I have heard many Members during the Budget debate talk about this and they have rightly pointed out that with the global spectre of inflation, some businesses may have legitimate reasons to raise prices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, our job in the CAP will be to look into errant practices that are flagged out by the public and bring to task those who unfairly profiteer using GST increase as a reason.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to ensure that businesses keep their prices transparent and do not misrepresent the reasons for any of their price increase.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The committee will share more details on its work in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) and its President Mr Melvin Yong for the strong partnership in safeguarding the interests of our consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We assure Mr Melvin Yong that we will review the constructive suggestions that he made yesterday to strengthen our consumer protection regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will work closely with CASE and the industry to better protect and empower consumers and at the same time, create greater opportunities for businesses in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, I would now like to take the opportunity to touch on another important group of businesses, one that is very close to our home, one that is very close to our hearts – our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Shawn Huang said it very well yesterday during the delivery of his cut.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: He said that our heartland enterprises are the heartbeat of our community and I completely agree with him because the shops in our heartlands form a central thread of Singapore's social fabric and our everyday lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Singaporeans grew up with these "mom and pop shops".

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They play an important role in our neighbourhood, providing convenience and affordable goods and services at our doorstep, as well as jobs for Singaporeans near their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartland spaces are also fertile ground for the birth and growth of many well-loved local enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, do you know that our very own homegrown bakery Bengawan Solo started out in an HDB block at Marine Terrace?

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the years, it has expanded to become a household name, serving both local and international customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With their affordable rent and ample pool of residents as customers, heartland spaces are ideal incubators for the next generation of notable Singaporean brands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many budding entrepreneurs have seized this opportunity and have launched their dreams in the heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We can now often find businesses with very fresh and very cool concepts in our neighbourhood, like gourmet burgers or even novel pets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I have come to know Mr Lee Syafiq of Ashes Burnnit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: He leads a very young team and he himself is only 30 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: He and his team serve up delicious gourmet burgers across four hawker centres and coffeeshops in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to do more to nurture and launch fresh waves of entrepreneurs in our very own heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In recent years, heartland enterprises face various challenges arising from changing consumer behaviour and rising competition exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue to work with our partners and not let up in our efforts to help our heartland shops stay competitive and stay relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of the key initiatives that we rolled out in October 2020 was the Heartlands Go Digital (HGD) programme, which aims to help our heartland enterprises respond to the COVID-19 situation and also adapt to new consumption patterns and leverage digital commerce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This progress is a great step forward for many of our "mom and pop shops" that were only using cash and operating strictly as a brick-and-mortar store just two years ago before the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartland enterprises truly deserve our admiration and our praise for their resilience and their can-do spirit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MTI and ESG will build on this momentum to bring our heartland enterprises onto a higher plane and into a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The four-year programme to energise and support heartland shops will seek to: one, deepen the digital and manpower capabilities of our heartland shops; and two, upgrade the capabilities of our TACs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Under this new roadmap, heartland enterprises will be equipped progressively via the Heartlands Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will accelerate our outreach to merchants and encourage them to take up solutions and training in financial and inventory management as well as venture into online sales through other e-commerce vendors and subsidised solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides digital capabilities, we will widen the reach of the current Heartlands Visual Merchandising Programme to increase their offline capabilities and attract customers and improve sales.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Another key thrust of Our Heartlands 2025 programme is to improve and deepen the capabilities of our TAC partners who are active in our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As I had mentioned earlier, TACs are important partners in helping our enterprises grow and transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To support the needs of our heartland enterprises and their transformation journey, we will strengthen and develop capabilities of the Federation of Merchants' Associations Singapore (FMAS) and the Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECS) as well as our local merchants' associations (MAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will free up more time and resources for the local merchants' associations to help their member shops adopt solutions to increase their revenue and to improve their efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, we are committed to helping our heartland shops gear up for the future through Our Heartlands 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the next few years, we hope to see them grow their revenue, boost their operational efficiency and attract new customers into our vibrant heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On that note, we are looking forward to the heartlands attracting more Singaporeans to eat, shop and spend using their Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: You may recall that about $130 million worth of vouchers were given out just about two months back in December 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More than 91% of the participating businesses have received CDC voucher transactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The number of participating outlets in the CDC voucher scheme has grown to more than 14,500.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are very heartened that our heartland merchants and hawkers recognise the benefit of the CDC vouchers and hope that Singaporeans will continue to support our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, may I have your permission to say a few words in Mandarin, please?

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, it has been a difficult two years for our SMEs due to the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During this time, the Government rolled out many initiatives and support measures not only to help SMEs overcome their operating challenges, but also to encourage all businesses to pursue transformation efforts, boost their productivity and improve their sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The package will: one, extend crucial support for businesses in these sectors to improve their productivity and equip them with the capabilities to pivot and transform, so as to stay competitive and relevant; and two, help companies hire and train more locals and optimise their manpower arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: When speaking of the Food Services and Retail sectors, we cannot leave out our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartland enterprises offer a myriad of goods and services at affordable prices, inject vibrancy into our neighbourhoods and offer employment to Singaporeans close to their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They are crucial to our economy and our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I earlier shared about the Heartlands Go Digital programme as well as the Heartland Visual Merchandising programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: After the introduction of these programmes, we have gathered and listened to feedback from the merchants and merchant associations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: After further consultation and planning, ESG and HDB will be launching Our Heartlands 2025, a four-year programme that aims to energise and further the development of our heartland shops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope they can innovate and better meet the diversified needs of customers and ever-changing consumer habits, and add to the unique character of our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Minister for Finance announced during Budget that we will be committing another $650 million in CDC vouchers, which will be distributed over 2022 to 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope the CDC vouchers will encourage Singaporeans to patronise neighbourhood shops and help the continuing recovery of our heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To date, 1.1 million households, which is about 90.6% of all Singaporean households, have claimed the CDC vouchers distributed last December, with more than $62 million redeemed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More than 91% of the 14,500 neighbourhood shops and hawker stalls on the scheme have logged at least one voucher transaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I hope more heartland merchants and hawkers can participate in this programme and benefit from it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our heartlands are not just places where we can eat and shop, but they are key nodes in our everyday lives where people can have warm and genuine interactions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government will continue to work closely with our key partners to create business opportunities for our heartland enterprises, instil vibrancy into the heartlands and build a more cohesive neighbourhood and community together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): Chairman, we have come a long way in our fight against the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Despite the challenges, the last two years have also brought new opportunities and growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This has been possible because of our Singapore can-do spirit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As long as we are on this path together, we can take courage and strength that we do not walk alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, let us chart our way forward and scale new heights as one Singapore.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second clarification is on the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP).

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Singapore is the chairman for this year and we read about interest from China and Taiwan.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank the Member for the two very important questions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is important for us to make sure that we continue to monitor and watch carefully, before opening up in a big way.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is also important to recognise that with all the measures that we have been put in place, we have been able to keep the critical cases low and ICU capacity has been kept manageable.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, the large number of cases also means that the hospitals are very, very busy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is important for us to ensure that the healthcare system is protected and to allow the patients to be taken care of properly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will then give us more capacity to open up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member is correct that it is important for our economy that we continue in our journey to living with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There are three aspects of our economic recovery that are very important.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, the safe management measures (SMMs) that we impose, have put a strain on many of our economic sectors, particularly the domestic-facing sectors, such as the F&B and retail sectors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They face significant challenges because of restrictions on gathering and the safe distancing measures that they have to put in place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we have to recognise that it is important for businesses to bring their workers together because there are many team efforts that cannot be done with workers working from home.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we need to progressively restore working onsite and this will help us to open up our economy and allow the economy to recover faster.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Third, which is also very critical, is our global connection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are a hub for business, for travel, for talent, for ideas, for investments.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And that is why we are continuing to open up our interconnectivity.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are bringing in more and more important visitors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are also allowing more workers to return from overseas, some of whom have returned to their home countries and are unable to come back.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The construction sector, for example, is still facing constraints and we hope to be able to bring back more of these workers through the opening of VTLs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the Committee of Supply of MOT, I am sure Minister S Iswaran will elaborate on this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: CPTPP is a very high standard trade agreement that requires its members to meet very stringent trade practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will benefit the global multilateral rules-based trading system.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, Singapore and CPTPP members welcome economies which are able to meet these high standards, including the US and other economies.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But whether the US is able to join the CPTPP is something that we will need to continue to discuss with and engage the US on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Beyond CPTPP, Singapore has also been encouraging the US to continue its engagement in the Asian region and in particular, ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have several collaborations already in place with the US.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One is the Partnership for Growth and Innovation which was announced during the visit of US Vice President.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is multilateral, it is not just between Singapore and the US.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We want to continue to explore platforms for collaboration between this region and the US, because the US' participation and engagement in this region and in the economy of this region is very important.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We certainly look forward to further collaboration between Singapore and the US, as well as the region and the US.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I have three clarification questions: two for Minister Gan and one for Minister Tan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For Minister Gan, he had gone into some detail in explaining the evolution of our economy toward exportable services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Just to help us get a better understanding, I wonder if he is able to give us some handle on the share of exports that are currently attributable toward services as opposed to more traditional goods.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I ask this in part because the traditional export-oriented industrialisation model for which Singapore subscribed to is such that it is targeted at goods export rather than services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And services export is a relatively new and under tested model.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: India and the Philippines come to mind and their experiences have not been as promising.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My second question has to do with FTAs and utilisation of these FTAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This goes down to 3% for the Jordan-Singapore FTA and as little as 0% for the Singapore-New Zealand and Singapore-Panama FTAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The premise of the question is whether we are devoting, perhaps, excess resources to signing new FTAs to the detriment of other positive initiatives by the Ministry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My third question is directed at Minister Tan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Here I wish to echo Member Foo Mee Har's call for expanding on demand productivity enhancement consultation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is in part because as a business school professor and also understanding the research, SME productivity shortfalls can actually be extensively explained by managerial deficiencies, such as old-school basics like proper inventory management and HR practices and bookkeeping, not so much the sexy tech upgrades that people often think of.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, here I wonder whether the Ministry will have some efforts to entail public-private partnerships in this particular aspect.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Chairman, I thank Assoc Prof Jamus Lim for the question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it constitutes a very important component of our total export and we will continue to help our companies to export our services.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned earlier in my speech, there are significant opportunities in the export of services, including the green economy as well as digital services.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In terms of the FTA utilisation, for FTAs, we have to look at it carefully.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the one hand, FTAs provide preferential access for our exports in terms of tariff savings because they allow us to have tariff-free access to important markets.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, that is an important savings for our businesses.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It means that, otherwise, they would have to pay $1 billion in tariffs to other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But FTAs are not just about tariff savings because they also provide greater transparency for the rules and regulations that will allow our businesses to be able to do business in these countries more easily.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Certain FTAs also provide protection in terms of our investments in these countries and that will allow our companies that have investments in these countries to have security with regard to their investment, to allow them to be able to operate freely within those markets.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think we have to look at FTAs in totality.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not just specifically on tariffs but it allows many other forms of access.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: A lot of these access may not be recorded, including protection of IPs and protection of investments.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And also, it provides a framework for data exchange.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of these are very critical to our businesses when they do business in other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, this is the overall benefit of FTAs for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Assoc Prof Lim's point for on-demand consultancy productivity, today, all our SMEs are welcome to drop into any of our SME Centres or Connect with ESG.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On an individualised basis, as I have said, we try to not just have bespoke advice for the larger enterprises but, to the extent that is possible, we try to cater and tailor it to SMEs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You can appreciate the fact that SMEs come from a very wide diaspora of different businesses, different sectors, different industries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, in terms of trying to help them, to reach them, there is not a one-size-fits-all perspective.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One of the examples that we have done is a company called Excelpoint Technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have all the details at this particular point in time to share, but I am happy to answer it separately.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Importantly, we welcome this type of public-private partnership.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If the hon Member Assoc Prof Lim can envisage that there are more of these partners, earlier on, towards the end of my speech, I have constantly encouraged SMEs to take that first step.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If there are partners who are willing to partner us to expand the range of service offerings for our own local enterprises, to bring them, to groom them, to develop them into large local enterprises and eventually, to become a Singapore global enterprise, I think we would very much welcome them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are all after the same thing in this aspect.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we are trying to do is to grow Singapore enterprises into large local enterprises (LLEs), put them on the world map and, at the same time, offer our Singaporean employees, our Singapore Core, a chance at being able to go global.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am heartened to hear about the plans for the ITM Refresh and Manufacturing 2030.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is exciting to hear how we are pioneering using additive manufacturing to repair state-of-the-art jet engine components.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Minister Gan mentioned that the ITM Refresh will consider workplace transformation and upskilling and retraining workers.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The reason for me asking this is that industries are already finding it hard to find the manpower to grow.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We must use the opportunity from the ITM Refresh to realise the latent potential from this group of individuals and we create not just jobs, but inclusive jobs for all.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And we retain the experience as we grow our industries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But, at the same time, as you change the business model, you have to redesign the jobs so that they fit into the new business model.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And I will be very happy for MTI to work together with MOM and the tripartite partners and the companies to embark on this journey of redesigning jobs for existing workers as well as senior workers, including the workers who are more experienced, to transform them so that we can provide them with new career opportunities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank the Ministers for their answers to my cuts earlier.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is good to hear Ministers' answers that there are efforts to build talent and manpower by sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But I would just like to follow up on work to enhance the supply of Singaporeans with the requisite skillsets.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In terms of the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP), I am looking at the website of WSG, which mentions that one of the purposes of capabilities transfer programme is to develop a sufficient supply of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question I have is in relation to Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since the Budget Statement was announced, a few things have happened, especially on oil prices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A lot of analysts are talking about the Russian oil price shock now, in terms of supply crisis, logistics crisis and payment crises and many crises that have emerged.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Chairman, I will take the first question and Minister Gan will take the subsequent question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The first point that Mr Saktiandi Supaat raised, it overlaps the auspices of MOM and MTI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is significant focus on expanding the Continuing Education and Training (CET) component, even for mid-career workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, under the WSG, we have invested significant resources in developing the Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The precursor was the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) and we have now morphed it into the CCPs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are very focused on making sure that we work with companies, we walk with companies, helping them to not just redesign skillsets as to what is necessary for them to pivot and to transform, but on top of that, we have our very close relationship with our tripartite partners.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: NTUC drives that part of it, together, in terms of working, reskilling and also training as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There will be other programmes, perhaps, if I can beg Member's indulgence to stay for the MOM Committee of Supply debate later.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You will see the whole plethora of programmes that we have available.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The impact, since the war started, has already been felt in many parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In Singapore, you can also see that energy prices have been on the rise.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As for commodities, some of the food suppliers are also indicating that their raw material costs have gone up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are beginning to feel the impact of the war in Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, I should also caution that it is still early days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have not felt the full impact of what the Ukraine crisis will have on the global economy as well as on Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Broadly, I can try to categorise the impact into three aspects.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Members may remember probably two years ago, even when the COVID-19 pandemic was ongoing, we were importing eggs from Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, in terms of supplies, the world will see a shortage of supply of products from Ukraine and Russia.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And secondly, the impact is not just on specific supplies, but also on supply chains.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Analysts have indicated that the supply chain, which is already very tight with challenges of the pandemic, now, coupled with the Ukraine crisis, will be tightened even further.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But the Minister for Finance has reassured all of us that we will continue to monitor the situation and if need be, we will provide more support and help for both businesses, our workers as well as our households.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we promoted domestic tourism and spending to achieve some resilience with locals and also to reduce our dependency on overseas visitors given the COVID-19 border closure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, lots of thanks to the Government for the vouchers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What can be done to further promote and strengthen to achieve less reliance on overseas visitors, and also, to have another pillar, that is, domestic spend?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not possible for us to support the entire population and our entire economy based on domestic consumption.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: During the pandemic, foreign visitor numbers dried up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We had significant barriers in terms of travel and tourists would not come because of the quarantine, the Stay-Home Notice (SHN) and all the border measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And therefore, we had to support our local industry, particularly the tourism industry, and we rolled out the SingapoRediscover Vouchers to help to spur demand for the local and domestic industry.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we cannot do this in perpetuity because we just will not be able to support local industry purely by spending our way through.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is therefore important for us to have a strategy which Ms Low Yen Ling has explained.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our tourism industry is preparing ourselves for the eventual recovery.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we need to continue to invest in our tourism sector, continue to invest in attracting foreign tourists to come to Singapore when the pandemic subsides.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is also important in the meantime to continue to see what we can do to help local industries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I am sure our CDC vouchers – which Ms Low may be prepared to elaborate in a short while – has gone a long way in helping our domestic economy, particularly the heartland shops, retailers and markets and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are rolling out additional CDC vouchers in the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will go towards helping our domestic industry cope with the current challenges.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we have to be quite clear in our mind that it is not possible for the Government to purely support the industry through tax revenues.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We need to continue to encourage our external economy, the export of both of our services and our goods, to be able to support our local economy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On this note, maybe Ms Low will be able to elaborate more on our CDC programmes in helping local industries.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Like what Minister Gan has mentioned and if everyone in the House remembers, about a year back, when Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the $130 million CDC vouchers, he cited two objectives.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The first objective was to thank fellow Singaporeans for their sense of solidarity during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He also highlighted the second objective, which is to stimulate demand for the products and services at our HDB shops and also by our hawkers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the last two years, our HDB shops and our hawkers have been adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic because they are the front-facing, consumer-facing businesses.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even though now, although dining has opened up, limited to five persons, certainly, in terms of traffic flow, some may say it is not as busy as before the COVID-19 period but necessarily so because of safe distancing measures.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, in the last nine months, the CDCs have been working with our Government agencies – and allow me to use this platform to thank the whole-of-Government effort in supporting our CDCs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: First, a big thank you to GovTech, the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO), IMDA – because we worked with IMDA and their SG Digital Office, with their digital ambassadors to support the onboarding of our HDB shops and our hawkers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This was timely because IMDA and MCI had earlier rolled out Seniors Go Digital and Hawkers Go Digital programmes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: By then, many Singaporeans and many hawkers and many seniors are very comfortable using mobile phones to scan a QR code and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I believe less than four weeks after the launch, we crossed the one-million mark.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: More than one million households claimed the vouchers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MTI and ESG have been working very closely with FMAS and HECS to conduct a survey on how this has supported and turbocharged the market.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are very heartened to hear from our HDB shops, merchants, hawkers saying that since the launch of the CDC vouchers in December – which also coincided with our inaugural Heartlands Festival which was launched on 28 November – it really brought human traffic, the crowd to the neighbourhood centres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is because we have designed it in such a way that it coincided with the festive period.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have heard from the merchants who are participating merchants and hawkers of the CDC Vouchers Scheme that their sales have improved 10%, some 30% and, in some cases, 40%.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, many merchants were very heartened to hear Minister Lawrence Wong announced two weeks ago when he delivered Budget 2022, that, this year, he will roll out another tranche of $130 million in CDC vouchers, which means that every Singaporean household will receive $100 of CDC vouchers under the Household Support Package (HSP).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we want to give assurance to Ms Foo Mee Har and Members in the House that in designing products and solutions like these, hand in hand with our HDB shops and our SMEs, if we bear in mind the objective, which is to stimulate demand for their products and services, the CDC Vouchers Scheme has shown – just like the SingapoRediscover Vouchers did – it can bring a multiplier impact to the economy.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Chairman, can I just make a quick clarification?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I mentioned $1 billion of tariff savings from our FTAs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That number was correct, but it was for 2020.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I said last year but, actually, it is for 2020.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Chairman, allow me to thank Minister Gan Kim Yong, Minister Tan See Leng and Minister of State Low Yen Ling for responding to our cuts and clarifications; and also wishing Minister of State Alvin Tan a speedy recovery.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Our economy is facing challenges and stresses from multiple fronts.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: But we take comfort that we have a best-in-class MTI team there and now helmed by Minister Gan, who is, of course, no stranger to managing crises.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We wish MTI all the best and, with that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
